catalog_quote: [p. 37] We are fortunate to have for Citak Asmat a tentative phonological analysis from an authoritative source: M. Bromley's reports on a suggested Citak orthography (1973, 1975). His analysis, although by no means final, shows that the Citak phonemic system is richer than that of any of the other Asmat languages. The following outline is based on Bromley's reports. The phoneme inventory tentatively set up by Bromley counts 16 consonants, 7 vowels, and 3 tonemes. ... If only bi-syllabic words are taken into account, the prosodic phenomena can be described as contrastive stress. However, on monosyllabic words Bromley found three contrastive pitch patterns: 1. short low or downglide; 2. short and high; 3. long upgliding high. The three tone patterns are more clearly recognisable in the Tiau dialect than in the Senggo dialect, Bromley observed. ... A similar system including some evidence…

new_statements.rule_in_words: No positional rule is given: in words of two (or more) syllables stress is described as contrastive/phonemic (i.e. lexically specified, not predictable by position), while monosyllables carry a three-way tonal (pitch/length) contrast; the analysis is Bromley's tentative one for the Senggo and Tiau dialects, relayed by Voorhoeve.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Voorhoeve stresses the analysis is 'by no means final'. In Senggo some speakers have merged tone patterns 1 and 2 or realise the contrasts as syllable length / 'ballistic' onset rather than pitch.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level prosody of isolated lexical words (orthography-report context); bisyllabic vs monosyllabic words distinguished; nothing on phrase level or on words longer than two syllables beyond 'polysyllabic words' having phonemic stress (7.2).
new_statements.identity_note: Voorhoeve's 'Citak Asmat (CI)' = Glottolog cita1245 (ISO txt; alt. Kaunak, Cicak, Tjitak, Asmat Darat). Bromley's analysis relayed by Voorhoeve is of the Senggo dialect with comparative remarks on the Tiau dialect, both Citak proper; Kruidhof 1979 describes the Tiau variety. Tamnim Citak (tml, tamn1235) is a separate Glottolog language and is NOT covered; the archive.org/PHOIBLE item 'tml_SPA1979_phon' labelled Tamnim Citak is actually SPA's Flamingo Bay Asmat (Voorhoeve 1965 = Central Asmat cent2117) and must not be used for either Citak code.

sources.note: Ch. 5.2 (p. 37), summarising Bromley's 1973/1975 mimeo reports: in bisyllabic words the prosody 'can be described as contrastive stress'; monosyllables carry three contrastive pitch patterns (tone), clearer in Tiau than in Senggo dialect. 3.1.2.3 (p. 22): 'a tonal system restricted to monosyllabic words, bi-syllabics having phonemic stress'; 7.2 (p. 43): 'phonemic stress in polysyllabic words and a tonal system restricted to monosyllabic words'. No rule of position given; stress is presented as phonemic/contrastive.
